exposure: Blastocyst morphology post-warming (degree of blastocoel re-expansion and post-warming cell survival)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 612 single vitrified-warmed blastocyst transfer cycles performed between November 2016 and May 2017, including 196 cycles with PGT-A tested embryos.
finding: Post-warming blastocyst re-expansion and high cell survival rate were significantly associated with higher live birth rates in both euploid and untested blastocysts.
